manualSections.title: Getting Started
manualSections.intro: The essentials to get the most out of your clipboard history every day.

cards.title: Open your history instantly
cards.body: Press Super + V (customizable in Shortcuts) or left-click the Mklipper icon in your taskbar.
cards.details: The global shortcut uses a lightweight D-Bus fast path to open the floating window right under your cursor with near-zero latency. Left-clicking the tray icon anchors the popup beside the panel while keeping it inside screen bounds; middle-clicking opens it at the pointer. You can also drag the window from any empty area to reposition it.

cards.title: One-tap paste (and Shift format override)
cards.body: Click any item, press Enter, or use keys 1 to 0 to paste directly into your active window. Hold Shift to invert formatting for a single paste.
cards.details: Mklipper automatically remembers the window you were working in before opening the popup, restores focus to it, and sends the right paste keystroke: Ctrl + Shift + V for terminals and Ctrl + V for regular apps. Holding Shift while clicking, pressing Enter, or using Alt/Ctrl + 1–0 temporarily inverts Paste without formatting for that paste only. In Settings → General you can enable persistent mode to paste several items in a row.

cards.title: Paste without formatting
cards.body: Toggle Paste without formatting at the top to strip colors, fonts, and HTML styles when pasting text. Images and files are never affected.
cards.details: When enabled, rich text copied from browsers, documents, or emails (HTML, RTF, custom fonts, and background colors) is automatically stripped to clean plain text — even on direct Ctrl + V — while screenshots and file paths remain untouched. You can also assign a global shortcut under Settings → Shortcuts to toggle it from any application.

cards.title: Tray icon counter, highlight & quick menu
cards.body: The tray icon displays a notification circle with the count of new items and briefly highlights them when you open the window. Right-click for the quick menu.
cards.details: Whenever new items are captured while the window is closed, a red notification circle shows the count (1–99 and 99+). Opening Mklipper resets the counter to zero and gives newly added items a subtle fade-out accent highlight so you can spot them immediately. Prefer the classic icon with no badge or highlight? Disable Show new items counter on the tray icon in Settings → General. Right-click opens pause capture, edit current, QR code, clear history, and settings.

manualSections.title: Cards
manualSections.intro: Search without worrying about accents, filter by type, preview large items, and use per-card quick actions.

cards.title: Accent-insensitive search & category filters
cards.body: Start typing as soon as Mklipper opens to filter instantly, or switch between All · Text · Images · Links · Pinned by clicking or pressing Tab.
cards.details: Search ignores letter case and diacritics/accents and supports multiple words in any order (for example, typing resume cafe matches “Café Résumé”). It searches across both the item content and its saved source app, window title, and URL. Press Tab anytime to cycle swiftly through all 5 category filters.

cards.title: Full preview & save images as PNG
cards.body: Press Space (or click the eye button) to inspect large screenshots or multi-line text without pasting, and save images directly as PNG.
cards.details: The preview view displays full multi-line text with character and line counts, or a large scaled image with exact pixel dimensions, without modifying your active clipboard. Right from the preview you can use the item, jump into the text editor, or export the screenshot using Save PNG (also available directly on image cards). Press Esc or Back to return to the list.

cards.title: Pin favorites & back them up
cards.body: Click the star on a card to protect important items when clearing history and access them via the Pinned filter.
cards.details: Pinned items are never purged when the history reaches its maximum size or when you clear history. Under Settings → General → Privacy & Backup, you can Export pinned… to a JSON file (including images, saved with private 0600 permissions) and Import pinned… on another machine without creating duplicates.

cards.title: Edit, QR code, source & capture time
cards.body: Hover over a card to edit text (Ctrl + Enter saves), generate a scannable QR code, or open the original source link.
cards.details: Each card displays a subtle metadata line showing the source app or domain and the relative time since it was originally captured (“Just now”, “10 min ago”, “Yesterday, 18:30”), updating live without resetting when reopening the window or deleting other rows. The offline QR code view lets you transfer links or snippets straight to your phone.

cards.title: Fast, safe deletion
cards.body: Click the trash button or press Del to remove an entry immediately, or use the top toolbar icon to clear non-pinned history.
cards.details: Both clearing history and deleting a pinned item ask for confirmation by default to prevent accidental loss (with a Do not ask again option). Remaining items keep all of their metadata and original capture timestamps intact.

manualSections.title: Actions
manualSections.intro: Automate quick workflows on copied text, such as opening links, files, or running custom commands.

cards.title: One-click links & local files
cards.body: When you copy a web URL (https://...) or an existing local file path, a bolt button appears on the card to open it with its default app.
cards.details: Mklipper automatically detects valid http/https URLs and existing local file paths, offering to open them directly in your browser, viewer, or file manager. You can disable this built-in detection under Settings → Actions if you only want custom rules.

cards.title: Optional automatic action menu
cards.body: Enable Automatic actions menu from the tray menu or Settings to pop up matching actions automatically right when you copy.
cards.details: In Settings → Actions you can configure how many seconds the popup stays visible before closing automatically (use 0 for no timeout), choose whether primary mouse selection triggers actions, strip leading/trailing whitespace before matching, and optionally replay actions when picking older history items.

cards.title: Custom regular-expression rules
cards.body: Create custom rules in Settings → Actions using regular expressions and shell commands with %s as the copied text.
cards.details: Each rule defines a regex pattern and one or more commands. The %s placeholder is safely passed to your command, and you can choose whether command output is ignored, replaces the current clipboard entry, or is added as a new history item (handy for formatting JSON, cleaning URLs, or transforming text).

manualSections.title: Shortcuts
manualSections.intro: Control everything from the keyboard with full support for standard, international, and gaming keyboards.

cards.title: Global shortcuts synced with Cinnamon
cards.body: In Settings → Shortcuts, assign keys to open history, toggle Paste without formatting, pause capture, edit, show QR, run actions, cycle, or clear.
cards.details: On Linux Mint Cinnamon, all 9 global shortcuts automatically synchronize with System Settings → Keyboard → Custom Shortcuts. Each shortcut invokes the running instance via D-Bus (--toggle, --toggle-plain-text, --toggle-pause, --edit, --qr, --action, --cycle-next, --cycle-prev, --clear-interactive) for instant execution.

cards.title: Quick keys inside the floating popup
cards.body: Use 1–0 for instant paste, Space for preview, Tab to switch category, Shift to invert format, and Del to remove.
cards.details: When the search box is empty, pressing 1–9 or 0 (10th item) pastes that row immediately; while searching, Alt + 1–0 and Ctrl + 1–0 still work. If you prefer typing digits straight into the search box, disable Use keys 1–0 for quick paste in Settings → Shortcuts. Also handy: Ctrl + F focuses search and Esc goes back or closes.

cards.title: Gaming keyboards & manual picker
cards.body: Mklipper recognizes macro keys (F13–F24) and any X11 layout. If the desktop intercepts Super, Ctrl, or Alt, use the keyboard picker beside the field.
cards.details: The X11 shortcut engine queries the live keymap and modifier map dynamically, avoiding mismatches on international or multi-layout setups. When recording a shortcut, the manual picker lets you toggle modifiers and select any key (including extended function keys F13–F24) even if your window manager intercepts the raw keystroke.

manualSections.title: Privacy
manualSections.intro: Your data stays under your control with zero telemetry, native Linux Mint integration, and clean disk deletion.

cards.title: Pause capture (incognito) mode
cards.body: Temporarily suspend clipboard recording from the pause button in the popup, the tray menu, or a global shortcut.
cards.details: While capture is paused, nothing you copy is saved or added to history, the tray icon switches to a muted pause badge, and the popup shows a clear banner with a Resume button so you never forget to turn recording back on.

cards.title: Passwords & ignored applications
cards.body: Secrets from compatible password managers (KeePassXC, Bitwarden, 1Password, etc.) and lockscreens are filtered automatically, plus you can add your own ignored apps.
cards.details: Mklipper honors standard password-manager secrecy hints and displays a discreet warning banner with a Clear button while a secret remains in the system clipboard — never writing it to disk. Screen lockers and polkit auth prompts are also ignored automatically, and under Settings → General → Privacy & Backup you can manage a custom ignored-applications list.

cards.title: Clean erasure & private permissions
cards.body: Every deleted entry is overwritten and immediately frees disk space, stored with private permissions restricted to your user.
cards.details: The SQLite database in ~/.local/share/mklipper/ runs with secure_delete = ON and auto_vacuum = FULL: deleting an entry or clearing history overwrites data pages, removes associated binary blobs, and purges orphaned files. History directories, settings, and JSON backups enforce strict 0700 / 0600 permissions. You can also turn off Keep history across sessions to wipe data on exit.

cards.title: Integrated Linux Mint updates
cards.body: Mklipper integrates with the Linux Mint Update Manager and notifies you whenever a new release is available.
cards.details: Installed via Mklipper's signed APT repository, updates arrive seamlessly alongside regular Mint system updates and Mklipper automatically restarts cleanly once the package upgrades. You can also check and install updates anytime from Settings → General → Check for updates now… with localized release notes and SHA-256 verification.
